title: Compressing horizontal distance but not height: a shader warp that makes distant landmarks loom above.
author: yaosio
selftext:
Try it here. This is just a tech demo. https://claude.ai/artifact/327mwcbU2kuKtvVVnSnXPe

While trying to create an effect I saw in an AI generate a video Claude Opus 5.5 came across this really neat effect. This is a real-time vertex warp. Past a set distance from the player, the world is pulled in horizontally but keeps its full height.

What it does depends on where you look. Anything above eye level, like a tower or a mountain, gets drawn closer but just as tall, so it looms over you and holds that height as you walk toward it. Anything below eye level does the opposite: from up high, the ground drops away steeply, so the world below looks much farther away than it really is.

It's one formula in the vertex shader, based only on where the player stands, so turning doesn't change anything. Objects crossing the boundary bend smoothly back into normal 3D.

Additionally a pixelated effect has been added along with dithering making it reminiscent of a 90s adventure game with really low res pictures. There is also a day night cycle.

comments.body: This looks really good. Creative thinking.

replies.author: yaosio
replies.body: Thanks! Claude managed to dechiper what I was saying to make it. It actually didn't do exactly what I said but that made it better.

comments.author: Last-Ad-8470
comments.body: This is totally how it feels in real life gj capturing that

replies.author: yaosio
replies.body: Thanks! This effect unexpectedly brought up nostalgic feelings about 90s games. Unfortunately I don't really have any ideas for games so I can't do much of anything with this. 😿

comments.author: RevalianKnight
comments.body: Now the next step is to make it look like hand crafted pixel art not 3d generated assets with a pixel filter that looks like ass

replies.author: yaosio
replies.body: That's a completely different look. Hand crafted pixel art is not pixelated. This look reminds me of early 90's games with dithered and pixelated digitized images as backgrounds.

replies.author: RevalianKnight
replies.body: Ah ok I misread. I thought you were going for that AI generated video look that was making rounds. The effect you made is very cool though. Curious though which early 90s games do you have in mind. Any examples?

replies.author: yaosio
replies.body: I don't remember their names but I do remember the look. I'm thinking of those games that use photos that they digitized which is very common in CD ROM adventure games. It's also possible I miss remembering things and I'm conflating different things that I remember from back then as something else.

comments.author: CodexPleaseReset
comments.body: Yeah wow this is awesome. I second the comment saying this is how it feels in real life. Like when you go hiking, and the mountains and views you see are just monstrous in a way that is never reflected in your photos. Yet, you've done it here. Nice work

comments.author: mattisverywhack
comments.body: Holy shit! Nice work. I feel like games have been trying to figure this out forever and you’ve done it
